issues.legal_issue: The reasonable annual rental value of a building for municipal rating cannot be based on rent actually received above the rent lawfully chargeable under rent-control law when a standard rent has been fixed.
material_facts: The dispute concerned the municipal assessment of a house for house-tax purposes under the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911.
A fair rent for the house had been fixed under the New Delhi House Rent Control Order, 1939, and that fixation remained valid; no later fair-rent or standard-rent fixation had occurred.
The landlord actually received rent substantially higher than the previously fixed fair rent.
The municipal assessment was enhanced on the basis of the rent actually received.
issues.conclusion: The actual rent received above the standard rent could not determine the rateable value. The assessment had to be based on the standard rent, subject to the applicable statutory deduction, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1)(b) of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 bases a building’s annual value on the gross annual rent at which it may reasonably be expected to let. Applying Corporation of Calcutta v. Smt. Padma Debi, the Court held that reasonable expectation must account for rent-control restrictions and their penal consequences: a landlord is presumed to act prudently and abide by the law, so unlawful excess rent cannot define the rental value for rating. The Court also referred to the rating principles in Patel Gordhandas Hargovindas v. Municipal Commissioner, Ahmedabad, and Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. M/s. Polychem Ltd. Sections 5(1) and 48(1)(a) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, prohibited claiming or receiving rent above standard rent and provided a penalty; the Court also considered the standard-rent framework in section 6 and explained that the proviso to section 116 of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, supported this understanding of reasonable rental value.

rule.if: municipal_house_tax_valuation_case and rent_control_limits_chargeable_rent and standard_rent_previously_fixed and no_later_rent_fixation and actual_rent_exceeded_standard

predicates.municipal_house_tax_valuation_case: The proceeding concerns the valuation of a building for municipal house-tax rating.
predicates.rent_control_limits_chargeable_rent: The applicable rent-control law limits the rent a landlord may lawfully claim or receive and attaches consequences to exceeding that limit.
predicates.standard_rent_previously_fixed: A fair or standard rent for the building was fixed under the applicable rent-control regime.
predicates.no_later_rent_fixation: No later fixation of fair or standard rent replaced the earlier fixation.
predicates.actual_rent_exceeded_standard: The landlord actually received rent above the fixed fair or standard rent.
predicates.rateable_value_based_on_standard_rent: The building’s rateable value is based on its fixed standard rent rather than unlawful excess rent actually received.

issues.definition: When a house-tax valuation dispute involves a building with an existing, unreplaced standard rent and the landlord received rent above the legally permitted limit, the valuation is based on the standard rent rather than the excess actually received.
